classic_upsell.name: Classic Upsell
classic_upsell.summary: The simplest upsell—offer something free or heavily discounted just for buying. Target 80%+ take rate when done seamlessly.
classic_upsell.hormozi_principle: You can't have X without Y. Make it feel like they're incomplete without the upsell.

tasks.description: Choose something that enhances what they just bought
tasks.principle: The upsell should make the original purchase MORE valuable

tasks.description: Determine how much you can discount while staying profitable
tasks.formula: Break-even = (Upsell Cost) / (Original AOV increase × Take Rate)
tasks.recommendation: Offer 70-90% off or FREE to maximize take rate

tasks.description: Position upsell as exclusive reward for customers
Customer should be able to add upsell with single click
tasks.requirement: Card already on file from main purchase
tasks.best_practice: No new checkout process, just 'Add to order'

tasks.description: Show upsell immediately after main purchase commitment
Allow skip without friction, but don't highlight it
tasks.example: Small 'No thanks' link below prominent 'Yes! Add to my order' button

tasks.description: Make them feel they're missing out without it
templates: One-time offer for new customers only

tasks.description: Display normal price vs. special price
Create reason to act now
examples: Never offered again at this price

tasks.description: Test different products, prices, and positioning
Measure: (Upsells Accepted / Main Purchases) × 100
tasks.target: If under 80%, the offer or presentation needs work

tasks.description: Try upsell at different points in customer journey

common_mistakes: Upsell requires too many steps (friction kills conversion)
Offer isn't compelling enough (needs to be 70%+ off or FREE)
Wrong timing—too early or too late in journey
Upsell is unrelated to main purchase
Making 'No thanks' too prominent
quick_wins: Start with FREE bonus product (100% take rate proves the mechanism works)
Test $1 upsell to validate demand before pricing higher
Implement order bumps (checkbox upsell) for 30-50% take rate

menu_upsell.name: Menu Upsell (Hormozi's Favorite)
menu_upsell.summary: The most sophisticated upsell using 4 tactics: Unselling (tell them what they DON'T need), Prescribing (tell them what they DO need), A/B Offer (ask preference), and Card on File (make it easy).

target_metrics.prescription_accuracy: Right product for customer 90%+ of time

menu_upsell.hormozi_principle: Prescribe, don't sell. Act like a doctor—diagnose their situation and prescribe the right solution.

tasks.description: For each customer type, determine which products to tell them to skip
tasks.principle: Telling someone NOT to buy something builds massive trust
tasks.example: You don't need our premium package because you're just starting. That's for people who already have X.

tasks.description: Write specific language for what to unsell to whom
tasks.format: 'Based on what you told me, you actually don't need [product] because [reason]. That's designed for [different situation].'

tasks.description: Most salespeople struggle to tell customers NOT to buy
tasks.key: This builds trust that makes them buy MORE overall

tasks.description: Map customer situations to right products
tasks.format: If customer has [situation A] → Prescribe [product X]. If [situation B] → Prescribe [product Y]

tasks.description: Questions to diagnose which products customer needs
examples: What's your biggest challenge right now?
Where are you in your journey?

tasks.description: How to present the recommendation
tasks.template: 'Based on what you told me about [their situation], I'd recommend [specific product] because [specific reason]. Here's why it's right for you...'

tasks.description: Create decision tree for which product to prescribe when
Always give two options and ask which they prefer
tasks.principle: Changes the question from 'Do you want this?' to 'Which one do you want?'

tasks.task: Create A/B pairs for each product
tasks.description: Every product should have a paired alternative
tasks.example: 'Would you prefer the standard package with X, or the premium with X and Y?'

tasks.description: Language for presenting both options
tasks.template: 'We have two options that could work for you. Option A gives you [benefits]. Option B gives you [different benefits]. Which feels more aligned with your goals?'

tasks.description: Save customer's card for future purchases
Once prescribed, customer can add with single confirmation
tasks.script: 'I'll add that to your account now. You'll see the charge on your next statement.'

tasks.description: No re-entering payment info, no cart abandonment

tasks.task: Train sales team on all 4 tactics
tasks.description: Role-play scenarios using Unsell → Prescribe → A/B → Card on File flow
Monitor: Did prescribed product lead to good customer outcome?
tasks.adjust: Refine diagnosis matrix based on results

tasks.description: Track: Testimonials, repeat purchases, referrals from menu upsell customers

common_mistakes: Selling instead of prescribing (pushing products vs. diagnosing needs)
Not having enough products to prescribe from (need 4+ products)
Asking 'yes or no' instead of 'A or B'
Not capturing card for easy future purchases
Skipping the unselling step (loses trust-building opportunity)
quick_wins: Start with just the A/B offer tactic (immediate improvement)
Add unselling to your next 5 sales calls (watch trust increase)
Save cards for all customers now to enable future one-click

anchor_upsell.name: Anchor Upsell
anchor_upsell.summary: Present the premium version FIRST at 5-10x the price, wait for the gasp, then 'rescue' them with your main offer—which now feels like a bargain.
anchor_upsell.hormozi_principle: Only change secondary features between anchor and main offer. The core transformation stays the same—premium just does it faster, with more support, or in a better format.

tasks.description: This is what you want most people to buy
Premium must be real value, not inflated fake tier
Same core outcome, different delivery method
tasks.principle: Never change the PRIMARY outcome—just how they get there

tasks.description: Some people WILL buy it (5-15%)
tasks.requirement: You must be able to deliver premium if they say yes

tasks.task: Present premium FIRST with full enthusiasm
tasks.description: Don't hold back—sell the premium like you want them to buy it
tasks.script: 'Let me show you our VIP program. This is our most comprehensive solution...'

tasks.description: No apologizing, no flinching
Pause and let them react to the price
Offer the main product as the affordable alternative
tasks.script: 'I totally understand. That's not for everyone. Let me show you something that might work better for where you are right now...'

tasks.task: Present main offer as the solution
tasks.description: Now your regular price feels like a bargain
Brainstorm everything that could justify 5-10x price
What does it actually cost you to deliver premium?
tasks.target: Premium should still have strong margins

tasks.description: Things only premium customers get
Write out exactly how to present premium → rescue with main
Role-play until presenting high prices feels natural

tasks.task: Track premium vs. main offer selection
tasks.description: Monitor: % who buy premium (should be 5-15%), % who buy main after seeing premium
Note what customers say when they hear premium price (useful for refining)

common_mistakes: Premium feels fake or inflated (customers see through it)
Can't actually deliver premium (what if they say yes?)
Apologizing for premium price (undermines the anchor)
Changing the core outcome between tiers (confuses customers)
Premium is only 2-3x main price (not enough anchoring effect)
quick_wins: Start by adding 1-on-1 access to create 5x premium tier
Practice stating high prices out loud until comfortable
Use anchor in proposals: Show premium budget first, then recommended option

rollover_upsell.name: Rollover Upsell
rollover_upsell.summary: Credit what customers already paid toward a higher-priced next offer (at least 4x higher). Hormozi's most-used upsell for reactivation and retention.
rollover_upsell.hormozi_principle: Works in 4 scenarios: Re-engage old customers, Rescue upset customers, Steal competitors' upset customers, Upsell current customers. The key is: next offer must be at least 4x the credit amount.

tasks.description: Must know exactly what each customer has spent
tasks.critical: Cannot do rollover without accurate tracking

tasks.description: Determine credit for each customer segment
Rollover only works if upgrade is significantly higher value
tasks.example: Customer paid $500 → Roll into $2,000+ offer (4x minimum)

tasks.description: Customers who purchased 6+ months ago and haven't bought since
Pull total spend for each dormant customer
Reach out with rollover offer
tasks.script: 'You invested $X with us before. We don't want that to go to waste. We'll credit that entire amount toward [premium offer] if you're ready to take the next step.'

tasks.description: 3-5 emails to re-engage with rollover offer
Customers who requested refund, complained, or canceled
Credit their investment toward better solution
tasks.script: 'I hear you're not happy with [product]. Rather than just refunding you, what if we credited that entire amount toward [better solution] that might be a better fit?'

tasks.task: Train support team on rescue protocol
tasks.description: When customer complains → Offer rollover before refund
Credit what they paid competitors toward your solution
tasks.script: 'Paid $X to [competitor] and didn't get results? We'll credit that toward our program.'

tasks.description: How customers prove what they paid competitors
options: Honor system for first X customers

tasks.description: Target competitor's audience with rollover messaging
Current customers ready for next level
Credit previous purchases toward premium tier
tasks.script: 'You've invested $X with us so far. We'll roll that toward [premium program], so you're already $X closer to your goal.'

tasks.description: Make rollover standard part of upgrade discussions
Track credits offered, accepted, and revenue generated
Prepare team to handle each rollover situation
Trigger rollover offers based on customer behavior
Track: Rollover offers made, accepted, revenue recovered

common_mistakes: No purchase history tracking (can't calculate credits)
Next offer isn't valuable enough (less than 4x credit)
Using rollover too frequently (diminishes effectiveness)
Not following up on rollover offers (need multiple touches)
Forgetting to include competitor switchover (missing market)
quick_wins: Start with dormant customer reactivation (lowest-hanging fruit)
Implement rescue protocol before refunds (save lost revenue)
Add rollover to every upsell conversation as standard practice
